title: How do you take your coffee? ☕🥛🍯 Improve your listening skills with Real Easy English

sentences.en: Hi Neil. How are you?
I'm very well thank you, Georgie.
Are you enjoying your coffee?
I am, but it's got a bit cool now.
I prefer my coffee hot, but...
oh well! Are you enjoying yours?
sentences.ko: 뭐 어쩔 수 없죠! 당신은 맛있게 마시고 있어요?

sentences.en: I've finished mine.
Oh, that's a shame.
It's a sad moment when I've finished my second coffee of the day, because that's it.
sentences.ko: 그날의 두 번째 커피를 다 마시면 슬퍼요. 그게 마지막이거든요.

sentences.en: I don't have more than two.
sentences.ko: 하루에 두 잔 넘게는 안 마셔요.

sentences.en: So, we're talking about coffee in this episode, aren't we?
sentences.ko: 그러니까 이번 에피소드에서는 커피에 대해 얘기하는 거죠?

sentences.en: We are. But before we start, of course, everyone needs to know that there is a free worksheet on our website.
sentences.ko: 네. 그런데 시작하기 전에, 웹사이트에 무료 학습지가 있다는 걸 다들 알아야 해요.

sentences.en: That's at bbclearningenglish.com.
Yes, they can also find a free transcript, can't they?
sentences.ko: 네, 무료 대본도 볼 수 있죠?

sentences.en: They can, yes, at the same address.
So, Georgie, we're talking about coffee.
sentences.ko: 자, 조지, 커피 얘기를 해 봐요.

sentences.en: How much coffee, or how many coffees if we're talking about cups of coffee – how many do you have a day?
sentences.ko: 하루에 커피를 얼마나, 잔으로 따지면 몇 잔 마셔요?

sentences.en: I usually have two, and I know that you do as well, because we drink them both in the office, don't we?
sentences.ko: 보통 두 잔이요. 당신도 그런 거 알아요, 우리 둘 다 사무실에서 마시잖아요.

sentences.en: We have one cup of coffee in the morning and one usually in the afternoon, when we need to regain some energy and alertness.
sentences.ko: 아침에 한 잔, 그리고 보통 오후에 기운과 정신을 되찾아야 할 때 한 잔 마셔요.

sentences.en: Yeah. And so, we all know because we make each other...
at BBC Learning English, we make each other coffee, so we know how we take our coffee.
sentences.ko: BBC Learning English에서는 서로 커피를 타 주니까, 각자 커피를 어떻게 마시는지 알아요.

sentences.en: Yes. 'How we take our coffee' is how we like it – what we like to put in it.
sentences.ko: 네. 'How we take our coffee'는 커피를 어떻게 좋아하는지, 뭘 넣어 마시는지를 말해요.

sentences.en: For example, sugar or milk.
I know that you don't like milk in your coffee.
sentences.ko: 당신은 커피에 우유 넣는 걸 안 좋아하잖아요.

sentences.en: You take your coffee black.
I do. I like black coffee and you take your coffee white and you used to have sugar, but you don't anymore.
sentences.ko: 네. 저는 블랙커피를 좋아하고, 당신은 우유를 넣어 마시죠. 예전엔 설탕도 넣었는데 이젠 안 넣고요.

sentences.en: That's right. Occasionally when I'm at home I put some honey in my coffee to make it a bit sweeter.
sentences.ko: 맞아요. 가끔 집에서는 커피에 꿀을 조금 넣어서 좀 더 달게 마셔요.

sentences.en: Eurgh! Honey in coffee?
Yes. Is that surprising?
I've never heard of that.
Really?
Sugar, but not honey.
But why would that be so bad?
Well, I don't know.
It's just I've never heard of it.
It's really good.
I would recommend.
OK. So, Georgie, what happens if you don't have your coffee?
sentences.ko: 좋아요. 조지, 커피를 안 마시면 어떻게 돼요?

sentences.en: Well, in the morning if I don't have coffee, I feel very grumpy and very tired.
sentences.ko: 음, 아침에 커피를 안 마시면 아주 짜증 나고 아주 피곤해요.

sentences.en: In the afternoon if I don't have a coffee, it's not terrible, but I would prefer to have my afternoon coffee.
sentences.ko: 오후에 안 마시면 그렇게 끔찍하진 않지만, 오후 커피는 마시는 게 좋아요.

sentences.en: How about you?
Yeah, I need my coffee, especially in the morning, but I don't have my coffee first thing in the morning.
sentences.ko: 네, 저도 커피가 필요해요, 특히 아침에요. 그런데 일어나자마자 마시지는 않아요.

sentences.en: Oh, interesting.
I have it, kind of, I don't know... work time – nine o'clock.
Why is that?
I think it's too strong, too powerful.
sentences.ko: 너무 진하고 너무 센 것 같아요.

sentences.en: Or maybe just the way I drink it.
sentences.ko: 아니면 그냥 제가 마시는 방식 때문일 수도 있고요.

sentences.en: What happens if you drink too much coffee?
sentences.ko: 커피를 너무 많이 마시면 어떻게 돼요?

sentences.en: Ooh, then it's difficult to sleep because of the caffeine.
Caffeine is that chemical in coffee and tea that makes you feel awake and alert.
sentences.ko: 카페인은 커피와 차에 들어 있는 화학 물질로, 잠이 깨고 정신이 들게 해요.

sentences.en: But too much means you're too alert.
sentences.ko: 그런데 너무 많으면 정신이 너무 말똥말똥해지죠.

sentences.en: I don't think that caffeine has a big effect on me.
sentences.ko: 저는 카페인이 저한테 큰 영향을 주는 것 같지 않아요.

sentences.en: I don't think I have trouble sleeping if I drink too much coffee.
sentences.ko: 커피를 많이 마셔도 잠드는 데 문제가 없는 것 같아요.

sentences.en: It's strange.
Yeah, because sometimes I'll have an espresso after dinner.
sentences.ko: 네, 가끔 저녁 먹고 에스프레소를 마시기도 하거든요.

sentences.en: Really?
Yeah. And I can still sleep.
That's crazy.
Yeah. Lucky me.
Lucky you!
Neil, have you ever tried to cut down on coffee?
sentences.ko: 닐, 커피를 줄이려고(cut down on) 해 본 적 있어요?

sentences.en: Cut down on... You mean have less?
No, I haven't tried to cut down on coffee, but I've tried to cut down on caffeine.
sentences.ko: 아니요, 커피를 줄이려고 한 적은 없지만, 카페인을 줄이려고 한 적은 있어요.

sentences.en: OK.
So, I...
For a while, I only drank decaffeinated coffee, or decaf, as we call it.
sentences.ko: 한동안 디카페인 커피, 우리가 '디캡'이라고 부르는 것만 마셨어요.

sentences.en: OK. And how was that?
Well, I didn't miss caffeine at the time, I don't think.
sentences.ko: 음, 그때 카페인이 그립진 않았던 것 같아요.

sentences.en: It lasted for a long time, but now I drink caffeine. I don't care.
sentences.ko: 꽤 오래 그렇게 했는데, 지금은 카페인 마셔요. 상관없어요.

sentences.en: OK. Neil, it's time to recap the vocabulary we used in the conversation.
sentences.ko: 좋아요. 닐, 대화에서 쓴 어휘를 정리할 시간이에요.

sentences.en: We used the verb 'take'.
So, Neil, how do you take your coffee?
I take my coffee black, and I know you take your coffee white.
sentences.ko: 저는 블랙으로 마시고, 당신은 우유를 넣어 마시는 거 알아요.

sentences.en: Yes. We also heard 'caffeine', which is the chemical that is in coffee, which makes you feel more awake.
sentences.ko: 네. 'caffeine'도 나왔죠. 커피에 들어 있는 화학 물질로, 더 깨어 있는 느낌이 들게 해요.

sentences.en: Yes, but you can also get decaffeinated coffee or tea – it means there's no caffeine.
sentences.ko: 네, 그런데 디카페인 커피나 차도 있어요. 카페인이 없다는 뜻이에요.

sentences.en: And we usually shorten that just to 'decaf' – decaf coffee.
sentences.ko: 그리고 보통 'decaf'로 줄여 말해요. 디캡 커피요.

sentences.en: Yes. We also heard the phrasal verb 'cut down on', which means you have less of something.
sentences.ko: 네. 'cut down on'이라는 구동사도 나왔는데, 뭔가를 덜 먹거나 덜 한다는 뜻이에요.

sentences.en: Yep. And you can also say 'cut back on'.
It means the same thing.
OK. Well, that is the end of this conversation about coffee in Real Easy English.
sentences.ko: 좋아요. 자, Real Easy English 커피 대화는 여기까지예요.

sentences.en: Yes, and if people want to watch more episodes of Real Easy English, what should they do?
sentences.ko: 네, Real Easy English 에피소드를 더 보고 싶으면 어떻게 하면 돼요?

sentences.en: They should go to our website, bbclearningenglish.com, where they can find a free worksheet to test what they've learned.
sentences.ko: 웹사이트 bbclearningenglish.com에 가면 배운 걸 확인할 수 있는 무료 학습지가 있어요.

sentences.en: Goodbye for now.
Goodbye!
